findings.title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript (XSS)
findings.body: `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')` injects the raw Referer header into a single-quoted JS string with no escaping. EmbedController#ensure_embeddable only validates the referer's *host*, so an attacker on the embeddable host (or anyone who can set an arbitrary Referer, e.g. a crafted request) can supply a referer like `http://host/x');alert(1);//` and execute arbitrary script in the context of the Discourse origin. Escape with `j`/`to_json` or build the target origin from scheme+host only.

findings.title: Invalid ERB/Ruby `<%- end if %>` breaks the view
findings.body: Line 6 contains `<%- end if %>`. `end if` with a bare `if` modifier and no condition is a Ruby syntax error, so rendering embed/best will raise instead of producing the page. It should simply be `<% end %>`.

findings.title: raw_html cook method stores unsanitized HTML, enabling XSS from feeds
findings.body: `cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the sanitizing render pipeline. TopicEmbed.import (used by Jobs::PollFeed on arbitrary RSS/ATOM content) passes feed HTML straight through with this cook method, and the embed view renders it with `raw post.cooked`. Any `<script>`/event-handler markup in a polled feed (or any content the feed author controls) becomes executable script on the forum. The HTML should be sanitized/whitelisted before being stored as cooked.

findings.title: import mutates the caller's contents string
findings.body: `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends in place to the string passed in by the caller. Callers that reuse or cache the string (e.g. retrying the import, or passing a frozen/literal string) will see the footer appended repeatedly, or get a RuntimeError on a frozen string. Build a new string instead (`contents = contents + ...`).

findings.title: create_table with force: true in migrations can drop existing tables
findings.body: `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` (and the same change made to 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) issues a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating. If the table already exists on an installation, running the migration silently destroys its data. Migrations should not use `force: true`.

findings.title: poll_feed assumes every feed item has `content`
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` will raise NoMethodError on nil for RSS 2.0 feeds that only provide `description` (SimpleRSS only populates `content`/`content_encoded` for Atom-style feeds). Since the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a single such feed permanently breaks polling. Fall back to `i.description`/`content_encoded` and skip blank items.

findings.title: Weak postMessage origin check using substring match
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of the configured Discourse URL (e.g. `http://disc` prefixes, or `https://x` if present inside the URL), and conversely rejects nothing reliably. Compare the event origin for exact equality with the Discourse origin instead.

findings.title: content_sha1 updated even when revise! fails
findings.body: `revisor.revise!` can return false (e.g. `should_revise?` false) or `@post.save` can fail validation silently, yet `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` runs unconditionally. The embed then records the new checksum while the post still holds the old content, so the update will never be retried on subsequent imports. Only update the sha when the revision actually succeeded.
